body.estimand_functional: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), where \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) is the independently defined Airy value and is to be certified by the corrected all-count diagonal

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. The proved comparator assigns units independently with \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\). The corrected prior is selected independently of the design, and the orbit reduction is exact at every fixed allocation count; uniform optimization over all counts remains open.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes; the exact response-count orbit retains all eight response types.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the observation is the assigned label together with its binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed on the unrestricted design. Positive local counts, positive exterior counts, and zero-count faces are separate required conclusions of the corrected bridge, so boundary allocations cannot be discarded by assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The compact transverse coordinate is a design-independent prior device orthogonal to the finite-population contrast; shrinking it while retaining uniform control of posterior denominators and allocation boundaries is part of the open proof.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the proved sharp result is currently the fixed-independent-design expansion with coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), together with the corresponding one-sided lower limit for the unrestricted deficit. The former widening polynomial tube is exactly refuted. Its replacement is an effective compact rational Airy spline-square prior: a rational interval ODE/Taylor oracle certifies the normalized energy and weighted tails, and a fixed-input evaluator computes exact ordered-field Bayes intervals and finite allocation-stratum maxima. The unrestricted sharp equality remains the target; its design-uniform all-count bridge and computable cross-sample tail majorant are open.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order and finite response-type programs, while the proved fixed-independent theorem identifies the Airy coefficient. No available result gives the reverse inequality for every outcome-independent dependent design. The missing step is a uniform corrected-prior Bayes bridge covering \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, all positive-count exterior allocations, and zero-count faces with one effective remainder.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), all eight response types and a nonzero transverse nuisance direction are needed because a scalar-path prior can be exploited by a pair-focused design. The scientifically meaningful unresolved question is whether unrestricted designs improve on the fixed allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) at second order.
project_justification.fill: The current verified contribution gives the exact response-alphabet geometry, a total fixed-independent Airy procedure, an effective normalized rational Airy-record algorithm, a genuine corrected transverse prior at every admissible input, an exact permutation-orbit Bayes reduction, and a terminating same-input ordered-algebraic evaluator. The proposed root theorem now states the precise all-count inequalities and monotone tail certificate still needed for the unrestricted sharp equality.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) provide the scalar two-arm Airy benchmark and feedback bounds, not a three-active-arm all-design converse. Hull (2026) is likewise a two-arm unrestricted result. The accepted parent supplies the exact finite orbit game, first-order value, second-order order, and same-sample certificates. The present verified steps adapt the spectral computation to a replayable rational interval ODE/Taylor oracle and carry a corrected nonzero-transverse prior through exact fixed-input evaluation. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) remain methodological comparators; neither is invoked as the missing finite-population, allocation-uniform bridge. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation, not a censored-outcome reanalysis.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label gap and the defeat of scalar-path priors do not determine the asymptotic design gap. The widening polynomial density is unusable because its exact scaled Bayes deficit grows at least linearly in its truncation radius. The corrected rational Airy family removes that obstruction and is effectively generated, but same-input exact maxima do not yield a cross-sample modulus. A proof must still expand the exact posterior risk uniformly through rare-type and zero-allocation boundaries; no Gaussian, Taylor, or normal-limit statement is assumed.
body.honest_scope: The unrestricted sharp equality at \(c^\dagger\) remains the advertised estimand functional but is open. Proved results are the fixed-independent sharp expansion, the unrestricted one-sided deficit bound, the effective normalized Airy record, and fixed-input exact Bayes and primal certificates. No growing-\(K\), uniform vanishing-weight, arbitrary-real computability, or equality-versus-strict-loss conclusion is claimed. The corrected root theorem is restricted to \(c^\dagger\) and requires a single verified machine with a monotone computable tail majorant; finite numerical extrapolation is not a substitute.
body.interpretation: For a prospective fixed-horizon three-regimen trial with a prespecified binary endpoint and contrast \(1:-1/4:-3/4\), the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) and its nonlinear Airy correction have a proved sharp second-order value within that fixed design. Exact finite corrected-prior intervals can be computed at a planned sample size. They must not yet be interpreted as certificates that no dependent or otherwise nonstandard outcome-independent design has a smaller worst-case risk.
